## 固定收益市場開篇觀點

油價再度飆升、生產者通膨堅挺，加上美國財政部選擇性執行債券買回，使等待通膨自行降溫的代價升高，美債因而大幅下跌。2年期殖利率上升15.5個基點至4.587%，5年期上升14.6個基點至4.763%，10年期上升12.2個基點至4.964%，30年期上升7.7個基點至5.367%。短端領跌，交易員將聯準會在9月16日會議升息的機率提高至約70%，並完全反映10月前升息一次。

長端殖利率逼近多年高點之際，殖利率曲線仍然趨平。2年與10年期利差收窄3.3個基點至37.7個基點，2年與30年期利差收窄7.8個基點至78個基點。這種走勢有別於純粹由財政或長天期債券供給引發的拋售：政府融資疑慮依然重要，但調整幅度最大的是對近期政策反應最敏感的年期。

能源是本次市場震盪的主要來源。荷莫茲海峽周邊遇襲，美國與伊朗衝突也顯示可能延長，加劇供應疑慮；布蘭特期油上漲約7.55%至每桶$108.85，WTI上漲約8.05%至$103.78。油價漲幅已足以改變實際通膨以及央行可能採取的因應。10年期損益兩平通膨率上升3個基點至2.417%，10年期實質殖利率則上升9.2個基點至2.547%。通膨補償確實增加，但名目殖利率的升幅主要來自政策進一步收緊的預期與資本競爭。

8月生產者物價報告進一步支持這波重新定價。最終需求價格較7月上升0.4%，年增5.4%；月增幅為5月以來最大，年增率也略高於5.3%的市場共識。最終需求商品價格大漲1.1%，其中能源上升4.2%，柴油上漲24.1%。核心PPI月增幅較溫和，為0.2%，低於0.3%的共識，但年增率加快至4.6%。排除食品、能源與貿易服務的指標月增0.3%、年增4.7%，顯示基礎生產者通膨仍遠高於符合聯準會目標的速度。

勞動市場數據未能提供多少抵銷作用。截至9月5日當週，初領失業救濟金人數由上修後的20.7萬小幅降至20.6萬，續領人數則由177.5萬降至177.4萬。裁員偏低本身不代表政策必須收緊，卻削弱了為保護就業而容忍新一波通膨壓力的理由。其後公布的成屋銷售則顯示高利率已開始壓抑經濟活動，銷售下滑2%，年率降至398萬戶，為逾一年最弱。

財政部首次擴大買回10年至20年期債券，也加劇市場跌勢。交易商雖提交$105億債券，財政部在最高$60億的額度中僅接受$51.9億。官員與分析師認為，未買足額度是因財政部拒絕價格欠佳的報價，而非缺乏購買能力；但對期待官方更積極吸收供給的投資人而言，結果仍令人失望。這也突顯支撐市場與維持價格紀律之間的矛盾：若要買滿額度，就必須接受較不利的報價。

相較之下，當日$220億的30年期美債標售展現強勁得多的民間需求。新債得標殖利率為5.308%，比標售前殖利率低2.7個基點，尾差為近五年第二佳。初級交易商僅承接創紀錄低點的2.2%，也是任何傳統美債標售的最低交易商承接比率。投資人願意在歷史高檔的絕對殖利率承接長天期債券，但這項需求仍不足以逆轉市場對通膨與聯準會風險的整體重估。

風險資產走弱，但未顯示融資市場失序。標普500指數下跌0.58%，那斯達克100指數下跌1.08%，費城半導體指數下跌2.66%。VIX升至17.84，美元指數上漲0.32%，黃金期貨則下跌1.28%。美國高收益債利差小幅擴大。整體而言，這是一場對名目成長、通膨與政策補償的劇烈重估，而非資金無序撤離信用市場。

## 油價與生產者物價使聯準會政策辯論提前

油價漲勢的規模與結構改變了近期政策考量。市場認為伊朗衝突愈來愈難化解，WTI自5月以來首次收於$100以上，布蘭特則逼近$109。沙烏地阿拉伯表示，其產量已降至1990年以來最低；區域航運路線周邊攻擊加劇，另有報導指伊朗正在重建飛彈能力。荷莫茲海峽的石油產品流量仍遠低於戰前水準，成品油出口的復甦又慢於原油運輸。

這項差異相當重要，因為柴油等成品油對企業成本與家庭通膨的影響，比原油基準價格更直接。生產者物價報告顯示傳導已經發生：8月柴油價格上漲24.1%，運輸與倉儲成本提高，機票與醫院服務價格也上升。當中多項服務成分會納入個人消費支出物價指數；不過，自9月30日公布的數據起，法律服務、軟體及投資顧問服務的計算方式將調整，因此不能機械式地由PPI推算聯準會偏好的通膨指標。

整體PPI月增0.4%，符合市場共識，但細項並未呈現溫和的通膨圖像。商品價格上漲1.1%，服務價格僅上升0.1%。貿易服務利潤率下降0.2%，顯示批發商與零售商並未透過利潤率將漲價全面擴散；然而，排除食品、能源與貿易服務的指標仍月增0.3%、年增4.7%。電子零組件與配件價格上漲3.4%，顯示除燃料之外，科技投資熱潮也在推高投入成本。

美債的反應因此同時反映通膨補償增加與實質政策預期收緊。10年期損益兩平通膨率上升3個基點，反映額外的能源衝擊；實質殖利率更大幅上升9.2個基點，則顯示市場預期，即使較高的政策利率無法直接恢復石油供給，聯準會仍可能因通膨擴散並持續的風險而採取行動。2年期殖利率上升15.5個基點、2年與30年期利差收窄7.8個基點，也使政策反應函數的調整成為曲線最主要的訊號。

聯準會的難題在於，對利率最敏感的產業已相當疲弱，其他需求來源卻相對不受影響。8月成屋銷售降至398萬戶的年率，是2024年秋季以來僅有的兩次低於400萬戶之一。南部、中西部與東北部銷售均下滑，西部則持平。30年期房貸利率連續第三週上升至6.76%，為2025年6月以來最高；15年期房貸利率也升至6.09%。

住宅供給雖有改善，主要原因卻是市場周轉仍低迷。待售成屋數量較一年前增加5.9%至162萬戶，為2019年11月以來最多；按照目前銷售速度，相當於4.9個月供給，為逾十年最高。房價中位數仍年增1.6%至$42.91萬，而且現有房貸中利率高於6%的比例不到四分之一，使許多屋主不願放棄成本較低的既有貸款。

人工智慧投資對利率的敏感度正好相反。巴克萊估計，超大型雲端服務業者將逾90%的營運現金流投入AI基礎設施，不太可能因融資成本上升50至75個基點而重新評估計畫。這種韌性削弱了傳統貨幣政策的傳導管道：只要資料中心、工程與非住宅投資繼續擴張，住宅市場收縮便不一定會造成同等廣泛的營建衰退。

這種情況也使家庭承受更大調整壓力。若關稅、石油與AI資本支出對升息的反應都很有限，貨幣緊縮便須更多透過消費、住宅及其他非必要活動發揮作用。成屋銷售顯示這項調整正在進行，但失業救濟金數據表明，影響尚未演變為廣泛的勞動市場惡化。對聯準會而言，就業面暫時幾乎沒有足以抵銷新一波通膨風險的證據。

跨資產交易也反映這項轉變。美債殖利率上升帶動美元走強；儘管地緣政治風險持續，黃金仍因實質殖利率升幅較大而下跌。股市連續第四個交易日走低，以科技股為主的那斯達克與半導體類股表現落後，因投資人同時面對較高的折現率與AI建設融資成本上升。比特幣進一步跌破$8萬，連續第四個交易日下跌，但仍處於2月以來的大致區間內。

石油庫存並未實質緩解地緣政治溢價。美國原油庫存僅減少39.1萬桶，低於預期的160萬桶降幅；汽油庫存意外增加126.9萬桶，餾分油庫存也增加208.7萬桶，與市場原先預期下降相反。這類國內供需狀況通常會壓抑油價，但市場更關注區域產量、航運與成品油供應所面臨的風險。

## 標售需求強勁仍未能壓住殖利率

當日兩項美債操作看似呈現矛盾結果，但區分價格與目的後便相互一致。買回的目的在改善舊券流動性，而非消除政府融資需求；30年期標售則是測試投資人是否願意按當時殖利率向政府投入新資金。財政部買進流通債券時嚴格篩選價格，投資人面對殖利率高於5.3%的新發長債時則積極認購。

擴大後的買回以10年至20年期券種為目標，最高額度為$60億，是先前操作上限的三倍。市場提交$105億債券，財政部接受其中$51.9億。財政部長Scott Bessent表示，財政部只會按有利價格買進債券，並認為投資人似乎不願交出長期持債。自2024年恢復買回以來的53次操作中，這僅是長天期操作第三次未買滿額度。

市場參與者仍將結果視為政府抑制殖利率努力所面臨的另一項限制。操作集中的20年期券種相對交換利率明顯走弱。若要買滿額度，財政部必須接受競爭力較差的報價，因此面臨兩難：是盡可能擴大當下買回金額，還是維持支付價格的紀律。

30年期標售則對民間需求提供更清楚的訊號。得標殖利率5.308%，較標售前水準低2.7個基點；初級交易商僅承接2.2%，意味最終投資人幾乎吸收整批債券。由於30年期殖利率已升至2007年以來未見的水準，且標售同時面對大量公司債與市政債發行競爭，這項結果格外強勁。

然而，這股需求不足以扭轉整體市場。30年期殖利率收盤仍上升7.7個基點至5.367%，10年期殖利率也逼近5%。強勁標售可以證明投資人認為特定殖利率具有價值；但只要油價、政策預期與債券供給仍在變動，就不能據此認定市場要求的殖利率不會繼續上升。

政府融資預測使供給問題持續受到關注。美國銀行估計，受聯邦政府年度利息支出五年內倍增至逾$1.2兆等因素影響，美債淨發行量可能由今年的$1.9兆增至2028年的約$2.3兆。總統Donald Trump另提議，若共和黨在11月3日期中選舉後保住國會兩院多數，將向美國成年公民每人發放$5,000，為財政前景增添另一項潛在支出。

這項提案須經國會授權，外界普遍認為成為法律的可能性不高，但規模仍相當可觀：約2.4億名合資格成年人意味成本接近$1.2兆。副總統JD Vance提出可用關稅收入支應，但國會預算辦公室估計，本財政年度迄今關稅收入僅$1,670億，且政府本財政年度支出將比收入多出$2.1兆。市場即時反應溫和，反映的是提案通過機率偏低，而非潛在成本不大。

市政債顯示，即使信用面未普遍惡化，較高的美債殖利率仍可與地方供給共同施壓。10年期基準市政債殖利率大漲15個基點至3.69%，為2025年4月以來最高；30年期上升14個基點至4.89%，創2011年以來最高。Alabama Toll Road, Bridge and Tunnel Authority發行約$38億，紐約大眾運輸系統發行約$7.78億，紐約市前一日則已出售約$16億一般責任債。市政債基金週三也流出約$4.6億，為2025年4月以來最大贖回。

因此，壓力既來自基準利率，也有市政債市場本身的因素。在再投資資金偏低、美債殖利率上升之際，投資人還須吸收大量州與地方政府發債。市政債殖利率升幅超過30年期美債，顯示隨供給累積，免稅債投資人要求更多發行讓利。

美國整體信用市場仍較有秩序。按配息調整後總報酬計算，存續期間較長的投資級債ETF LQD下跌約0.90%，HYG與JNK則分別下跌約0.46%及0.43%。高收益債利差小幅擴大，但沒有跡象顯示市場普遍關閉。存續期間較長的已開發市場公司債與新興市場主權債指數跌幅接近1%，與政府公債殖利率大幅上升一致。

## 歐洲央行帶動全球重新定價能源風險

歐洲央行將存款利率提高25個基點至2.5%，這是伊朗戰爭爆發以來第二次升息。總裁Christine Lagarde形容這項一致通過的決定相當直接，並強調在歐洲央行三種經濟情境下都站得住腳。對市場而言，更大的意外來自預測與政策指引：投資人判斷這次升息並非一次性的因應。

歐洲央行預測，通膨率將在2026年達3%、2027年為2.5%、2028年為2.1%。在第2季經濟季增0.6%、成長基礎廣泛後，央行將2026年成長預測上調至0.9%，並表示第3季經濟活動可能仍具韌性。Lagarde警告，能源成本上升將逐步傳導至食品與核心通膨，使整體通膨率到2027年上半年仍遠高於目標。

隨市場提高進一步緊縮的預期，德國公債遭到拋售。2年期殖利率一度上升14個基點至3.21%，為近三年最高；10年期上升6個基點至3.50%，創2009年以來最高。交換市場完全反映到2027年中前再升息三次、每次25個基點，並認為10月升息的機率超過70%。

歐洲央行官員私下認為可能還需進一步緊縮，但也覺得市場完全反映三次升息或許過於積極。若能源價格持續偏高，10月可能採取行動；等到12月，決策官員則可取得延伸至2029年的新一輪預測。這項差異意味管理委員會維持鷹派立場，卻未認同市場定價所反映的完整升息路徑。

法國的財政溢價進一步加重歐洲債市跌勢。投資人同時考量歐元區政策利率上升以及預算與選舉的不確定性，法國10年期公債相對德國的利差盤中擴大至91個基點，為2012年以來最高。Lagarde也駁斥總統候選人Jean-Luc Mélenchon取消法國央行與歐洲央行所持法國政府債務的提議，警告拒絕償付官方持債將損害國家信用與未來融資成本。

英國市場的重新定價更為劇烈。10年期英國公債殖利率上升10個基點至5.378%，為2007年7月以來最高；20年及30年期殖利率分別升至5.895%與5.948%，均創1998年以來最高。對政策較敏感的5年期殖利率上升15個基點至4.95%，2年期則升至4.87%。儘管市場預期英格蘭銀行下次會議將按兵不動，定價仍顯示11月前升息的機率達97%。

英國標售£50億、票息4.625%、2030年5月到期的公債，平均得標殖利率為4.786%，是該期限區間自2023年10月以來最高。標售證明政府仍能發債，但融資成本已明顯提高。與此同時，住宅調查中回報房價下跌的仲介多於回報上漲者；2年期固定房貸平均利率也由美國與伊朗衝突前的4.83%升至5.67%。

日本的政策方向也變得更明確。日本央行審議委員Kazuyuki Masu表示，基礎通膨趨勢已接近2%，金融環境仍屬寬鬆，因此利率應繼續上升。他主張，正常化應使政策利率明確進入日本央行估計的1.1%至2.5%中性區間，讓決策官員可隨情勢變化向任一方向調整。

Masu支持在9月18日會議升息25個基點至1.25%，但不贊成迅速連續升息，也未支持一次升息50個基點。他表示，即使燃料、化學品、航運費與肥料成本使物價壓力擴大，日本央行仍不預期基礎通膨會突然大幅超標。交換市場認為9月升息的機率約為97%。

日圓在本月稍早上漲後，於美國交易時段下跌0.5%。巴克萊警告，若日本央行未帶來鷹派意外，或市場預期日本退休基金轉向國內資產的配置調整未成真，日圓可能回到每美元兌150多日圓的偏弱區域。匯率先前的漲勢已反映預期中的升息，因此政策指引以及9月以後的升息步調，比首次行動更為重要。

土耳其面對同一能源衝擊時採取不同反應。在年通膨率降至低於預期的31.5%後，央行將一週期利率維持在37%，符合市場幾乎一致的預測。決策官員承認國內需求轉弱、基礎通膨放緩，但仍將能源價格偏高列為上行風險。分析師認為，只有油價趨穩且通膨前景未惡化，央行才可能在10月22日會議降息；其中一項估計認為降幅可能為100個基點。

印度央行則透過外匯市場而非政策利率收緊流動性。油價及美元需求壓迫盧比，使其下跌0.3%至每美元兌95.44盧比。國營銀行賣出美元，可能是代印度央行操作；央行也連續第二個交易日進行美元兌盧比先賣後買換匯，使用9月及12月到期合約。這些操作抽走多餘的盧比流動性，推動1年期隱含遠期利率兩天內上升近30個基點至3.37%，為5月底以來最高。

## AI發債供給重塑信用債相對價值

AI投資週期帶來的影響已不只是公司債發行量增加，也正在改變美國投資級債內部、新興與已開發市場發行人之間，甚至同一借款人條件近似債券之間的相對價值。

法國巴黎銀行估計，超大型雲端服務業者明年可能發行約$4,000億債券，並預測固定收益市場淨供給總額將創下$3.7兆紀錄。該行策略師認為，在各國政府大量發債之際，信用債正由稀缺轉向充裕。他們預測年底前利差溫和擴大，美國投資級債約擴大7個基點、歐元債約6個基點；但更重要的是其結構性判斷：需求成長可能追不上資料中心及其他AI基礎設施所需的融資供給。

過去一年，Alphabet、Amazon、Meta、Microsoft與Oracle合計已發行約$2,200億債券。個別債券比較顯示，發行規模與新券供給壓力可能壓過新基準券通常具有的流動性優勢。Oracle票息5.95%、2055年9月到期的新券，流通額為$350億，8月21日殖利率為7.86%；票息4.375%、2055年4月到期的舊券流通額僅$100億，殖利率卻較低，為7.67%。新券利差比舊券寬22個基點。

Alphabet、Meta與Nvidia的類似債券也呈現相同逆轉，新發且規模較大的券種，利差比舊券寬15至22個基點。流通額達$350億至$400億的債券，規模位居美國投資級債市場最大的1.5%之列。如此龐大的供給造成顯著吸收壓力，足以抵銷一般應有的流動性溢價。

這項供給效應也縮小了美國科技借款人與亞洲新興市場信用債之間的差距。SK海力士2031年到期債券的殖利率僅比可比Amazon債券高9個基點，差距約為一年前的三分之一。騰訊2031年到期債券的利差與Apple相近期限債券大致相同，儘管穆迪對Apple的評級高出四個級距。台積電2031年到期美元債的利差則比可比Meta債券窄近20個基點，兩者評級同為Aa3；兩年前，台積電債券的利差還寬約25個基點。

這些比較不代表亞洲科技債一概便宜。部分投資人認為目前利差過窄，若超大型雲端服務業者大量發債迫使美國科技債利差進一步擴大，他們準備轉向美國債券。亞洲企業本身也有未來融資需求，包括承諾對晶片與資料中心進行大型投資的中國網路公司及南韓企業集團。目前的相對優勢來自供給較有秩序與本地需求強勁，而不是亞洲發行人不受AI資本密集特性影響。

Oracle仍是市場疑慮的核心。其2027財政年度資本支出預計接近$930億，比前一年增加逾65%，2028財政年度更將超過$1,040億；2027財政年度自由現金流預估為負$466億。標普已將公司評級降至投資級最低一級，違約保障成本也升至紀錄高點。收盤後公布的雲端業務成長優於預期，帶動Oracle股價上漲約6%，但投資人仍需看到營收與利潤率能夠追上融資負擔的證據。

這與主權債市場存在直接連動。美國投資級債發行進度較2020年高7.6%，而當年發行額曾創下$1.75兆紀錄。本週預計發行$700億，截至週三已完成$610億。油價與央行政策推高市場要求的實質殖利率之際，公司借款人與美國財政部正在爭奪同一批長天期資金承接能力。

對體質較弱的借款人而言，解決方案不只是提高利差，而是增加債權人保護。Sophos在再融資方案中加入omniblocker條款，限制公司向特定貸款人提供優先交易；方案另含Serta blocker，以防止透過非按比例換債使既有債權人的受償順位下降，以及Pluralsight blocker，防止智慧財產權被移出貸款人共同擔保範圍。

這套方案擬以約$167億新債為2027年3月到期的$210億貸款再融資，新債定價為基準利率加碼5至5.25個百分點，發行價為面額的97%，另有一筆€3.5億貸款。公司也將透過私募發行$30億以債付息（PIK）次順位工具，並投入$9.8億現金，以協助降低槓桿。整套方案仍屬低財務約束，但新增的特定阻擋條款，是公司對同時憂慮AI顛覆及激進負債管理交易的貸款人所作實質讓步。

Emeria的談判也取得進展。這家法國房地產服務公司及其股東討論注資約€3.5億，高於今年稍早考慮的約€2億；主要債權人則已簽署保密協議。Emeria的€36億負債中，部分可能移至控股公司，從而降低營運公司的債務，而不必對部分有擔保債權減記。債權人也要求取得英國業務的質押。條款仍可能變動，而在公司上半年虧損€1.08億、負債自2027年起陸續到期之際，再融資仍相當迫切。

Merlin Entertainments已取得£6.57億新貸款承諾，部分由倫敦眼及其他英國景點提供擔保。該融資的受償順位將與既有有擔保債務相同，用於處理即將到期的負債，包括2027年到期、等值$84億的無擔保美元與歐元債券。交易仍須滿足相關條件，預計年底前完成，因此屬於已進入後期的再融資，而非已經取得的最終資金。

## 主權融資管道與本地市場改革仍具選擇性

塞內加爾債務重整正朝有組織的債權人談判推進。近$500億歐洲債券的部分持有人已選定White & Case擔任法律顧問，同時研議債權人委員會的組成。Morgan Stanley Investment Management與BlueBay Asset Management是曾參與討論組成團體的投資人。塞內加爾尋求依強化版G20共同框架處理債務之際，這項委任為債券持有人提供正式法律平台。

政府表示，在此過程中將繼續償付債券，包括9月13日到期的2048年歐洲債券票息$3,370萬。塞內加爾也已就一項$220億IMF計畫達成工作人員層級協議。支付票息將維持近期履約紀錄，但債權人團體開始成形，也顯示投資人正為如何最終分配債務減免的艱難談判預作準備。

延宕的IMF計畫恢復推進，使薩爾瓦多朝相反方向發展。IMF已就第二次與第三次檢討達成工作人員層級協議，執行董事會核准後可撥款約$1.4億。自7月底以來，薩爾瓦多美元債報酬率達2.3%，優於拉丁美洲其他主權債，利差也收窄至2010年以來最低。

政府提交文件，顯示第一次檢討後累積的比特幣來自私人捐贈，而非公共資源，藉此回應與IMF之間的一項核心爭議。5月及6月經濟活動也都較一年前成長5.2%。目前剩餘的難題是退休金改革，預計延至明年，又受到2月總統大選影響而更為複雜。若IMF執行董事會在10月初前核准合併檢討，薩爾瓦多僅付息債券的票息將由4%降至0.25%。

目前估值幾乎不容許延誤。薩爾瓦多債券相對美債利差約271個基點，相較之下，評級相近的阿根廷約為500個基點，迦納則為218個基點。如此收窄的利差，已假設政府會持續執行計畫、及時取得核准，並推進退休金赤字改革；私人退休基金應收利息的寬限期將在2027年結束，屆時問題會更加迫切。

日本主權信用前景面對的是另一種財政考驗。惠譽表示，下次預算與基本財政收支路徑，將是評估首相高市早苗擴張政策的核心。政府在結合初始預算與追加支出的框架下，預算申請規模創下紀錄，同時借款成本持續上升。惠譽預期，名目成長與稅收將抵銷擴張政策，使債務占GDP比率未來五年持續下降，之後才趨於穩定。因此，其A評級與穩定展望是在有利的債務動態、政策執行與預算結構之間取得平衡。

智利則宣布一項旨在降低本國流動性溢價的市場結構改革。持有約$450億國債、占市場約40%的退休基金，將首次獲准進行附買回與附賣回交易。新制可讓基金以證券為擔保取得現金，或以高品質擔保品配置短期流動性，同時增加可供次級市場交易的債券。

這項改革是為改善異常低迷的市場。相對於近$1,100億的流通額，交易所登記的主權債日均交易額僅約$2.7億。九檔債券占登記成交量的80%，另有11檔債券今年完全沒有交易。央行發現，智利10年期債券買賣價差比墨西哥、巴西與哥倫比亞更寬。開放附買回交易，加上另一項造市商計畫，可能逐步改善價格發現，但不會立即帶動殖利率下降。

智利的改革與東南亞標售所受壓力形成對比。馬來西亞8月標售2046年到期債券，投標倍數為1.63倍，是今年第二低。泰國9月2日標售2036年到期債券，投標倍數僅1.13倍，為5月以來10年期債券最弱；菲律賓5年期債券標售的投標倍數則創2013年以來最低。印尼傳統公債標售收到66兆印尼盾投標，為7月7日以來最少。

儘管機構投資人仍看好區域經濟基本面，全球殖利率上升、油價走高與本地發債仍對長天期債券造成壓力。馬來西亞10年期殖利率本季已上升逾50個基點；泰國與菲律賓10年期殖利率則分別上升約20個基點及逾40個基點。泰國與印尼8月通膨率分別達2.53%及3.19%，均高於預期。

外部壓力也延伸至匯率與國內流動性。印尼已連續四個月吸引外資買進債券，但速度較6月的$13億流入放緩；9月7日，外資更出現一個月來最大的單日債券淨流出。印度以外匯換匯抽走流動性的作法，也顯示即使不升息，石油衝擊仍可經由另一條管道收緊金融環境。

並非所有新興市場借款人的融資管道都在惡化。MercadoLibre發行$10億、2036年到期的優先無擔保票據，票息5.850%、殖利率6.139%，資金用於一般企業用途。Vodafone Idea則與由印度國家銀行領軍的銀行團達成約$350億債務融資協議，用於重建網路。這筆期限接近十年的融資要求Kumar Mangalam Birla留任董事長，並包含違約時的還款保證，將公司治理與股東支持直接寫入信用條款。

## 後續市場意義

9月11日公布的美國8月CPI，是判斷石油衝擊仍集中於整體物價、或已開始擴散的近期關鍵測試。市場共識預期整體通膨月增0.4%，高於前月的0.1%，年增率則維持3.4%。核心通膨預計月增0.2%，年增率由2.5%放緩至2.4%。若核心讀數受控，市場對聯準會9月16日升息所賦予的70%機率將下降；若漲價壓力廣泛加速，則會加劇短端拋售，並強化市場對10月前升息的預期。

同日稍晚公布的密西根大學初值，將顯示能源成本是否不只推高當期通膨，也開始改變家庭預期。消費者信心預計由51.7降至51；前次1年期通膨預期為4%，5年期為3.3%。相較於信心單獨再度惡化，較長期通膨預期若上升，對政策更為重要，因為這代表燃料衝擊正影響民眾對即期漲價以外的看法。

8月月度預算報告預計顯示赤字約$4,040億，前值為$4,320億。在每人發放$5,000的提案與財政部干預市場的討論再起後，這項數據的重要性已經提高。發放款項仍以選舉結果與國會批准為條件，但預算數據將更新財政起點，讓市場據以評估任何新增支出。

美債供給將於9月15日恢復，屆時標售20年期債券，前次得標殖利率為5.204%。30年期標售表明，只要殖利率夠高，投資人願意吸收長天期債券。接下來要觀察的是，CPI公布後需求是否仍然積極，以及財政部選擇性買回是否改變市場對後續操作的預期。

9月16日的聯準會決策、經濟預測與記者會仍是最重要的政策事件。市場需要判斷，若升息成真，這會被視為對新一波通膨的一次性因應，還是較長緊縮週期的開始。油價、生產者物價與穩定的失業救濟金數據，均提高了維持利率不變所需的條件；CPI將決定基礎通膨是否跨過這道門檻。

歐洲央行的下一步雖非迫在眉睫，卻已重新成為市場的實際風險。官員認為可能繼續收緊；若能源價格維持高檔，10月便可能行動，12月則能取得更完整的預測。若薪資與服務通膨繼續放緩，市場目前反映的三次額外升息可能過度；但如今需要證明的，已是能源衝擊不會持續。

日本央行將於9月18日接棒。升息25個基點至1.25%幾乎已完全反映在價格中，因此政策指引將決定日本殖利率與日圓能否保有近期的政策溢價。Masu支持繼續正常化，但未暗示會升息50個基點，也沒有表達12月必須緊接升息。若例行升息搭配謹慎指引，市場對快速緊縮的預期將受挑戰；若央行明確承諾繼續朝中性區間推進，則會印證較長的升息週期。

多項信用事件仍有明確的執行風險。塞內加爾9月13日支付票息與否，將考驗政府在共同框架談判期間維持債務償付的承諾。薩爾瓦多仍等待IMF執行董事會核准合併檢討；若10月初前獲准，其僅付息債券的票息可能下降。Sophos、Emeria與Merlin則須把提案與債權人承諾轉化為完成的再融資交易。

利率與信用市場共同面對的考驗，已不再是有沒有買家。30年期美債標售、公司債發行與新興市場交易均顯示資本仍然可得。尚未解決的問題是：當油價推升通膨、央行收緊政策、政府大量發債，而AI建設又形成異常集中的民間融資潮時，買方會要求多少補償與保障。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries sold off sharply as a renewed oil surge, firm producer inflation and a selective Treasury buyback raised the cost of waiting for inflation to subside. The 2-year yield rose 15.5 basis points to 4.587%, the 5-year climbed 14.6 basis points to 4.763%, the 10-year gained 12.2 basis points to 4.964%, and the 30-year increased 7.7 basis points to 5.367%. The front end led as traders lifted the probability of a Federal Reserve increase at the Sept. 16 meeting to about 70% and fully priced a move by October.

The curve therefore flattened even as long-term yields approached multiyear highs. The 2s10s spread narrowed 3.3 basis points to 37.7, while 2s30s compressed 7.8 basis points to 78. The pattern distinguished the session from a purely fiscal or duration-supply selloff: government borrowing concerns remained important, but the largest adjustment occurred in maturities most exposed to a near-term policy response.

Energy supplied the dominant shock. Brent futures rose about 7.55% to $108.85 a barrel and WTI gained about 8.05% to $103.78 as attacks around the Strait of Hormuz and evidence of a prolonged U.S.-Iran conflict intensified supply fears. The price of oil had moved far enough to alter both realized inflation and the prospective reaction of central banks. The 10-year breakeven rose 3 basis points to 2.417%, while the 10-year real yield increased 9.2 basis points to 2.547%. Inflation compensation widened, but expectations of tighter policy and competition for capital accounted for most of the nominal yield increase.

The August producer-price report reinforced that repricing. Final-demand prices rose 0.4% from July and 5.4% from a year earlier, the strongest monthly increase since May and slightly above the 5.3% annual consensus. Final-demand goods prices jumped 1.1%, led by a 4.2% rise in energy and a 24.1% increase in diesel fuel. Core PPI rose a milder 0.2% on the month, below the 0.3% consensus, but accelerated to 4.6% annually. The measure excluding food, energy and trade services increased 0.3% on the month and 4.7% from a year earlier, leaving underlying producer inflation well above a pace consistent with the Fed’s objective.

Labor data offered little offset. Initial jobless claims edged down to 206,000 in the week through Sept. 5 from a revised 207,000, while continuing claims slipped to 1.774 million from 1.775 million. Low layoffs did not by themselves require tighter policy, but they reduced the case for tolerating renewed inflation pressure to protect employment. Existing-home sales later showed where higher rates were already constraining activity, falling 2% to a 3.98 million annual pace, the weakest in more than a year.

Treasury’s first expanded purchase of 10- to 20-year debt compounded the decline. The department accepted $5.19 billion against a maximum of $6 billion even though dealers offered $10.5 billion. Officials and analysts attributed the shortfall to Treasury rejecting unattractive prices rather than a lack of capacity to buy, but the outcome disappointed investors looking for more aggressive official absorption. It also showed the tension between market support and value discipline: filling the maximum would have required accepting less favorable offers.

Private demand was considerably stronger at the day’s $22 billion 30-year auction. The new bonds were awarded at 5.308%, 2.7 basis points below the pre-auction yield, the second-largest through in five years. Primary dealers received a record-low 2.2% of the sale, also the smallest dealer share for any conventional Treasury auction. Investors were willing to take long duration at a historically high outright yield, but that demand did not reverse the broader repricing of inflation and Fed risk.

Risk assets weakened without signaling a funding breakdown. The S&P 500 fell 0.58%, the Nasdaq 100 lost 1.08%, and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped 2.66%. The VIX rose to 17.84, while the Dollar Index gained 0.32% and gold futures fell 1.28%. U.S. high-yield spreads widened modestly. The session’s character was a forceful repricing of nominal growth, inflation and policy compensation rather than a disorderly flight from credit.

## Oil and Producer Prices Pull the Fed Debate Forward

The scale and composition of the oil move changed the immediate policy calculation. WTI closed above $100 for the first time since May, while Brent approached $109 as markets judged the Iran conflict increasingly difficult to resolve. Saudi Arabia reported that its production had fallen to the lowest since 1990, attacks around regional shipping routes intensified, and Iran was reported to be rebuilding missile capacity. Product flows through the Strait of Hormuz remained well below prewar volumes, with refined-fuel exports recovering more slowly than crude shipments.

That distinction matters because diesel and other refined products reach business costs and household inflation more directly than the crude benchmark alone. The producer-price report showed the pass-through already under way: diesel prices rose 24.1% in August, transportation and warehousing costs increased, and airfares and hospital services also advanced. Several of those service components feed into the personal consumption expenditures price index, although changes to the calculation of legal services, software and investment advice beginning with the Sept. 30 release complicate a mechanical translation from PPI into the Fed’s preferred gauge.

The headline 0.4% monthly PPI increase matched consensus, but the details did not present a benign inflation story. Goods prices rose 1.1%, compared with only 0.1% for services. Trade-services margins fell 0.2%, suggesting that wholesalers and retailers did not broaden the increase through margins, yet the measure excluding food, energy and trade services still rose 0.3% and remained at 4.7% annually. Electronic components and accessories increased 3.4%, showing that the technology-investment boom was also contributing to input pressure beyond fuel.

The response in Treasuries was correspondingly divided between inflation compensation and tighter real policy expectations. The 3-basis-point rise in the 10-year breakeven acknowledged the additional energy impulse. The larger 9.2-basis-point increase in the real yield reflected the likelihood that the Fed would respond to the risk of broader persistence even though higher policy rates cannot directly restore oil supply. The 2-year yield’s 15.5-basis-point increase and the flattening of 2s30s by 7.8 basis points made that reaction-function adjustment the dominant curve signal.

The Fed’s difficulty is that its most rate-sensitive sectors are already weak while other sources of demand remain comparatively insulated. Existing-home sales fell to a 3.98 million annual rate in August, one of only two readings below 4 million since the fall of 2024. Sales declined in the South, Midwest and Northeast and were unchanged in the West. The 30-year mortgage rate rose for a third week to 6.76%, its highest since June 2025, while the 15-year rate increased to 6.09%.

Housing supply improved, but largely because turnover remained subdued. The number of previously owned homes for sale rose 5.9% from a year earlier to 1.62 million, the most since November 2019. At the current sales pace, that represented 4.9 months of supply, the highest in more than a decade. The median sales price still increased 1.6% from a year earlier to $429,100, and fewer than a quarter of outstanding mortgages carried rates above 6%, leaving many owners reluctant to relinquish cheaper existing loans.

Artificial-intelligence investment presents the opposite sensitivity. Barclays estimated that hyperscalers were spending more than 90% of operating cash flow on AI infrastructure and were unlikely to reconsider projects because financing costs rose by 50 to 75 basis points. That resilience weakens a traditional monetary transmission channel: housing can contract without producing an equally broad construction downturn when data-center, engineering and nonresidential investment continue to expand.

The same dynamic raises the burden on households. If tariffs, oil and AI capital expenditure respond only weakly to higher rates, monetary restraint must work more heavily through consumption, housing and other discretionary activity. Existing-home sales showed that adjustment in progress. Claims showed it had not yet become a broad labor-market deterioration. For the Fed, that combination left little immediate employment evidence to counter the renewed inflation risk.

Cross-asset trading reflected the shift. The dollar advanced as U.S. yields rose, while gold declined despite continuing geopolitical risk because real yields increased more sharply. Equities fell for a fourth consecutive session, with the technology-heavy Nasdaq and semiconductor shares underperforming as investors confronted both higher discount rates and the rising cost of financing the AI buildout. Bitcoin fell further below $80,000, continuing a four-session decline, though it remained within the broad range that has prevailed since February.

Oil inventories did not materially relieve the geopolitical premium. U.S. crude stocks declined only 391,000 barrels, less than the 1.6 million-barrel draw expected, while gasoline inventories unexpectedly rose 1.269 million barrels and distillate stocks increased 2.087 million against expectations for a decline. Those domestic balances would normally restrain prices, but the market focused instead on the risk to regional production, shipping and refined-product availability.

## Strong Auction Demand Fails to Put a Ceiling on Yields

The day’s Treasury operations delivered apparently conflicting results that were consistent once price and purpose were separated. The buyback was designed to improve liquidity in older securities, not to remove the government’s financing requirement. The 30-year auction tested whether investors would supply new cash to the government at prevailing yields. Treasury was selective when purchasing outstanding debt, while investors were aggressive when offered a new long bond above 5.3%.

The expanded buyback targeted the 10- to 20-year sector and had a $6 billion maximum, three times the cap used in earlier operations. Treasury accepted $5.19 billion from $10.5 billion submitted. Secretary Scott Bessent said the department buys bonds only at favorable prices and argued that investors appeared reluctant to surrender long-term holdings. It was only the third time among 53 operations since buybacks resumed in 2024 that officials did not fill the amount for a long-duration operation.

Market participants nevertheless treated the result as another limit on the administration’s effort to restrain yields. The 20-year sector, where the operation was concentrated, cheapened particularly sharply against swaps. Filling the maximum would have required Treasury to accept less competitive offers, creating a choice between maximizing immediate purchases and maintaining discipline over the prices paid.

The auction produced a clearer signal about private demand. The 5.308% award was 2.7 basis points through the pre-sale level, and primary dealers received only 2.2%, meaning end investors absorbed almost the entire issue. The result was especially strong because the 30-year yield had reached levels last seen in 2007 and because the sale competed with heavy corporate and municipal issuance.

The demand was not sufficient to turn the broader market. The 30-year yield still ended 7.7 basis points higher at 5.367%, while the 10-year approached 5%. A strong auction can show that investors find value at a particular yield without establishing that the required yield will stop rising when oil, policy expectations and debt supply continue to change.

Government financing projections kept the supply question active. Bank of America estimated net Treasury issuance could rise to about $2.3 trillion in 2028 from $1.9 trillion this year, partly because annual federal interest expense has doubled over five years to more than $1.2 trillion. President Donald Trump added another potential claim on the fiscal outlook by proposing a $5,000 payment to adult U.S. citizens if Republicans retain both chambers of Congress in the Nov. 3 midterm elections.

The proposal would require congressional authorization and was widely considered unlikely to become law. Its scale was nevertheless material: roughly 240 million eligible adults would imply a cost near $1.2 trillion. Vice President JD Vance suggested tariff revenue as a funding source, but the Congressional Budget Office put fiscal-year-to-date tariff receipts at $167 billion and estimated the government would spend $2.1 trillion more than it collects in the current fiscal year. The muted immediate market reaction reflected the proposal’s low enactment probability, not a small potential cost.

Municipal bonds demonstrated how higher Treasury yields and local supply could combine even without a broad deterioration in credit. The 10-year benchmark municipal yield jumped 15 basis points to 3.69%, the highest since April 2025, while the 30-year rose 14 basis points to 4.89%, its highest since 2011. The Alabama Toll Road, Bridge and Tunnel Authority sold about $3.8 billion, New York’s transit network issued roughly $778 million, and New York City had sold about $1.6 billion of general-obligation debt the previous day. Municipal funds also lost about $460 million on Wednesday, the largest withdrawal since April 2025.

The pressure was therefore both benchmark-driven and market-specific. Investors had to absorb heavy state and local issuance while reinvestment flows were low and Treasury yields were rising. The municipal move exceeded the increase in the 30-year Treasury yield, showing that tax-exempt buyers demanded additional concession as supply accumulated.

Broad U.S. credit remained more orderly. The LQD investment-grade fund lost about 0.90% on a distribution-adjusted total-return basis, reflecting its greater duration, while HYG and JNK fell about 0.46% and 0.43%. High-yield spreads widened modestly, but there was no evidence of generalized market closure. Longer-duration developed-market corporate and emerging-market sovereign bond indexes declined close to 1%, consistent with the sharp rise in government yields.

## The ECB Leads a Global Repricing of Energy Risk

The European Central Bank raised its deposit rate by 25 basis points to 2.5%, its second increase since the Iran war began. President Christine Lagarde described the unanimous decision as straightforward and emphasized that it was robust across the ECB’s three economic scenarios. The larger market surprise lay in the projections and guidance: investors concluded that the move was not an isolated response.

The ECB projected inflation at 3% in 2026, 2.5% in 2027 and 2.1% in 2028. It upgraded 2026 growth to 0.9% after a broad-based 0.6% quarterly expansion in Q2 and said activity likely remained resilient in Q3. Lagarde warned that higher energy costs would feed gradually into food and core inflation and keep the headline rate well above target through the first half of 2027.

German bonds sold off as markets raised expectations for further tightening. The 2-year yield rose as much as 14 basis points to 3.21%, its highest in almost three years, and the 10-year climbed 6 basis points to 3.50%, its highest since 2009. Swaps fully priced three additional quarter-point increases by the middle of 2027 and assigned more than a 70% probability to an October move.

ECB officials privately judged that more tightening was likely but viewed three fully priced moves as potentially aggressive. October was considered possible if energy prices stayed elevated, while December would give policymakers a new set of forecasts extending into 2029. The distinction leaves the Governing Council hawkish without endorsing the complete market path.

France added a fiscal premium to the European selloff. The French 10-year spread over Germany widened intraday to 91 basis points, its highest since 2012, as investors combined higher euro-area policy rates with budget and election uncertainty. Lagarde also rejected presidential candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon’s proposal to cancel French government debt held by the Bank of France and ECB, warning that repudiating official holdings would damage the state’s credibility and future borrowing costs.

The UK experienced an even sharper repricing. The 10-year gilt yield rose 10 basis points to 5.378%, its highest since July 2007. The 20- and 30-year yields reached 5.895% and 5.948%, their highest since 1998, while the policy-sensitive 5-year rose 15 basis points to 4.95% and the 2-year reached 4.87%. Markets priced a 97% probability of a Bank of England increase by November even though the Bank was expected to hold at its next meeting.

A £5 billion sale of 4.625% May 2030 gilts cleared at an average yield of 4.786%, the highest for that maturity range since October 2023. The auction confirmed that the government could place debt, but at a substantially higher funding cost. Housing surveys simultaneously showed more agents reporting falling prices than increases, and the average 2-year fixed mortgage rate had risen to 5.67% from 4.83% before the U.S.-Iran conflict.

Japan’s policy direction also became more explicit. Bank of Japan board member Kazuyuki Masu said rates should continue rising because the underlying inflation trend was close to 2% and financial conditions remained accommodative. He argued that normalization should place the policy rate firmly within the BOJ’s estimated neutral range of 1.1%-2.5%, giving officials room to move in either direction as conditions change.

Masu supported the case for a quarter-point increase to 1.25% at the Sept. 18 meeting but did not endorse a rapid sequence or a 50-basis-point move. He said the BOJ did not expect an abrupt overshoot in underlying inflation, even as fuel, chemicals, shipping fees and fertilizer costs broadened price pressure. Swaps assigned about a 97% probability to the September increase.

The yen slipped 0.5% during the U.S. session after rallying earlier in the month. Barclays warned that a return toward the upper 150s per dollar was possible if the BOJ failed to deliver a hawkish surprise or if anticipated shifts by Japanese pension funds toward domestic assets did not materialize. The currency’s rally had already incorporated the expected hike, leaving guidance and the pace beyond September more important than the first move.

Turkey presented a different response to the same energy shock. The central bank held its one-week rate at 37%, matching the near-unanimous forecast, after annual inflation slowed more than expected to 31.5%. Policymakers acknowledged weaker domestic demand and slower underlying inflation but cited elevated energy prices as an upside risk. Analysts saw room for a cut at the Oct. 22 meeting only if oil stabilized and the inflation outlook did not worsen, with one estimate placing a possible reduction at 100 basis points.

India’s Reserve Bank tightened liquidity through the currency market rather than its policy rate. The rupee fell 0.3% to 95.44 per dollar as oil and dollar demand weighed on the currency. State-run banks sold dollars, likely for the RBI, while the central bank conducted dollar-rupee sell-buy swaps for a second consecutive session using September and December maturities. The operations drained excess rupee liquidity and helped push the 1-year implied forward rate almost 30 basis points higher over two days to 3.37%, its highest since late May.

## AI Supply Reorders Credit Relative Value

The AI investment cycle is no longer only increasing the volume of corporate bonds. It is changing relative value within U.S. investment grade, between emerging- and developed-market issuers, and even between nearly identical securities from the same borrower.

BNP Paribas estimated that hyperscalers could issue about $400 billion of bonds next year and projected total net fixed-income supply of a record $3.7 trillion. Its strategists argued that credit was moving from scarcity to abundance at the same time governments were issuing heavily. They forecast modest spread widening by year-end—about 7 basis points in U.S. investment grade and 6 basis points in euros—but the more important claim was structural: demand growth may not keep pace with the supply required for data centers and other AI infrastructure.

Roughly $220 billion of debt had been issued over the preceding year by Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft and Oracle. Bond-level comparisons showed that size and recency could overwhelm the liquidity advantage usually associated with a new benchmark issue. Oracle’s 5.95% September 2055 bond, with $3.5 billion outstanding, yielded 7.86% on Aug. 21, compared with 7.67% for its older 4.375% April 2055 issue with only $1 billion outstanding. The newer bond’s spread was 22 basis points wider.

Comparable bonds from Alphabet, Meta and Nvidia showed the same reversal, with newer and larger securities trading 15 to 22 basis points wider than older issues. Bonds with $3.5 billion to $4 billion outstanding rank among the largest 1.5% of the U.S. investment-grade universe. Their scale has created absorption pressure substantial enough to outweigh the ordinary liquidity premium.

That supply effect has also narrowed the distinction between U.S. technology borrowers and Asian emerging-market credits. SK Hynix’s 2031 bonds yielded only 9 basis points more than comparable Amazon debt, about one-third of the gap a year earlier. Tencent’s 2031 bond traded at roughly the same spread as Apple’s equivalent maturity even though Apple is rated four notches higher by Moody’s. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing’s 2031 dollar note traded nearly 20 basis points tighter than Meta’s comparable bond despite both carrying Aa3 ratings; two years earlier, TSMC had traded about 25 basis points wider.

The comparison did not mean Asian technology debt was uniformly cheap. Some investors judged those spreads too tight and were prepared to rotate toward U.S. bonds if hyperscaler issuance forced further widening. Asian companies also face their own future funding needs, including Chinese internet firms and South Korean conglomerates committed to large investments in chips and data centers. The present advantage reflects more orderly supply and strong local demand, not immunity from the capital intensity of AI.

Oracle remained at the center of the concern. Its capital spending was expected to approach $93 billion in fiscal 2027, more than 65% above the preceding year, and exceed $104 billion in fiscal 2028. Free cash flow was projected at negative $46.6 billion in fiscal 2027. S&P had downgraded the company to the lowest investment-grade rating, and the cost of default protection reached a record. Better-than-expected cloud growth after the close lifted Oracle shares about 6%, but investors still needed evidence that revenue and margins would catch up with the financing burden.

The interaction with sovereign markets is direct. U.S. investment-grade issuance was running 7.6% above the 2020 pace, when a record $1.75 trillion was sold, and the week’s expected $70 billion calendar had reached $61 billion by Wednesday. Corporate borrowers and the Treasury are competing for the same duration capacity just as oil and central-bank policy lift the required real yield.

For weaker borrowers, the answer has been more creditor protection rather than simply a higher spread. Sophos added an omniblocker to its refinancing package, restricting the company from offering preferential deals to selected lenders. It also included a Serta blocker against non-pro-rata exchanges that subordinate existing creditors and a Pluralsight blocker preventing the transfer of intellectual property away from the lender group.

The package would refinance a $2.1 billion loan due in March 2027 with roughly $1.67 billion of new debt priced at 5 to 5.25 percentage points over benchmarks and issued at 97 cents, plus a €350 million loan. A $300 million privately placed payment-in-kind junior instrument and $98 million of cash would help reduce leverage. The package remained covenant-lite, but the specific blockers marked a meaningful concession to lenders concerned about both AI disruption and aggressive liability-management transactions.

Emeria’s negotiations also advanced. Major creditors signed non-disclosure agreements as the French real-estate services company and its owners discussed a roughly €350 million equity injection, up from about €200 million considered earlier in the year. Some of Emeria’s €3.6 billion of liabilities could be shifted to a holding company, lowering operating-company debt without a partial secured write-off. Creditors also sought a pledge over the UK business. The terms could still change, and the urgency remained substantial after a €108 million first-half loss and with liabilities beginning to mature in 2027.

Merlin Entertainments secured commitments for £657 million of new loans backed partly by the London Eye and other UK attractions. The facility would rank alongside existing secured debt and address looming maturities, including the equivalent of $840 million of unsecured dollar and euro bonds due in 2027. Completion remained subject to conditions and was expected by year-end, making the transaction an advanced refinancing rather than closed funding.

## Sovereign Access and Local-Market Reform Remain Selective

Senegal’s restructuring moved toward organized creditor negotiations. Some holders of nearly $5 billion of eurobonds selected White & Case as legal adviser while they worked on the composition of a creditor committee. Morgan Stanley Investment Management and BlueBay Asset Management had been among investors discussing a group. The appointment gives bondholders a formal legal platform as Senegal seeks treatment under an enhanced version of the G20 Common Framework.

The government said it would continue servicing its notes during the process, including a $33.7 million coupon on 2048 eurobonds due Sept. 13. Senegal also reached a staff-level agreement for a $2.2 billion IMF program. Payment of the coupon would preserve near-term performance, but the creditor group’s formation showed that investors were preparing for difficult negotiations over the ultimate allocation of relief.

El Salvador moved in the opposite direction as its delayed IMF program resumed. A staff-level agreement on the second and third reviews could release about $140 million after executive-board approval. Dollar bonds returned 2.3% from late July, outperforming Latin American sovereign peers, while spreads narrowed to their lowest since 2010.

The government supplied documents indicating that Bitcoin accumulated after the first review came from private donations rather than public resources, addressing a central dispute with the IMF. Economic activity also expanded 5.2% from a year earlier in both May and June. The remaining difficulty is pension reform, now expected next year and complicated by February’s presidential election. If the IMF board approves the combined reviews by early October, the coupon on El Salvador’s interest-only notes would fall to 0.25% from 4%.

Valuations leave little room for delay. El Salvador traded at a spread of about 271 basis points over Treasuries, compared with nearly 500 for similarly rated Argentina and 218 for Ghana. The compression assumes continued program execution, timely approval and progress on a pension deficit that becomes more pressing when a grace period on interest owed to private pension funds ends in 2027.

Japan’s sovereign-credit outlook carried a different kind of fiscal test. Fitch said the next budget and primary-balance path would be central to its assessment of Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s expansionary program. Budget requests reached a record under a framework combining initial and supplementary spending while borrowing costs were rising. Fitch expected debt relative to GDP to keep declining for five years as nominal growth and tax receipts offset expansionary policy, then stabilize. Its A rating and stable outlook therefore balanced favorable debt dynamics against execution and budget composition.

Chile announced a market-structure reform intended to reduce its own liquidity premium. Pension funds, which own about $45 billion of Treasury bonds and roughly 40% of the market, will be allowed to conduct repos and reverse repos for the first time. The change should let funds raise cash against securities or invest short-term liquidity against high-quality collateral, while making more bonds available for secondary trading.

The reform addresses an unusually inactive market. Exchange-registered sovereign trading averaged about $270 million a day against nearly $110 billion outstanding. Nine bonds accounted for 80% of registered volume, and 11 instruments had not traded during the year. The central bank found 10-year bid-ask spreads wider than those of Mexico, Brazil and Colombia. Repo access and a separate market-maker program could improve price discovery gradually rather than produce an immediate fall in yields.

Chile’s change contrasted with the pressure at Southeast Asian auctions. Malaysia’s August sale of 2046 notes drew a bid-to-cover ratio of 1.63, its second-lowest of the year. Thailand’s Sept. 2 sale of 2036 debt achieved 1.13, its weakest 10-year cover since May, while a Philippine 5-year auction had the lowest coverage since 2013. Indonesia’s conventional auction drew 66 trillion rupiah of bids, the least since July 7.

Higher global yields, oil and local issuance were weighing on long maturities even though institutional investors remained constructive on the region’s economic fundamentals. Malaysia’s 10-year yield had risen more than 50 basis points during the quarter, while 10-year yields in Thailand and the Philippines increased roughly 20 and more than 40 basis points. August inflation reached 2.53% in Thailand and 3.19% in Indonesia, both hotter than expected.

The external pressure also reached currencies and domestic liquidity. Indonesia had attracted foreign bond buying for four consecutive months, but the pace slowed from June’s $1.3 billion inflow and foreign investors recorded their largest net bond outflow in a month on Sept. 7. India’s use of FX swaps to drain liquidity showed another route through which the oil shock could tighten financial conditions even without a rate increase.

Not every emerging-market borrower faced deteriorating access. MercadoLibre raised $1 billion through senior unsecured notes due in 2036 with a 5.850% coupon and 6.139% yield, using proceeds for general corporate purposes. Vodafone Idea obtained an agreement for about $3.5 billion of debt from a State Bank of India-led group to rebuild its network. The nearly 10-year financing requires Kumar Mangalam Birla to remain chairman and includes repayment guarantees in a default, placing governance and sponsor support directly into the credit terms.

## Forward Market Significance

August U.S. CPI on Sept. 11 is the immediate test of whether the oil shock remains concentrated in headline prices or is broadening. Consensus calls for a 0.4% monthly increase in headline inflation after 0.1%, with the annual rate holding at 3.4%. Core inflation is expected to rise 0.2% on the month and slow to 2.4% from 2.5% annually. A contained core reading would temper the 70% probability assigned to a Sept. 16 Fed increase; broader acceleration would reinforce the front-end selloff and the market’s expectation of a move by October.

Preliminary University of Michigan data later on Sept. 11 will show whether energy costs are altering household expectations as well as current inflation. Consumer sentiment is expected to slip to 51 from 51.7. The prior 1-year inflation expectation was 4%, and the 5-year measure was 3.3%. A rise in the longer measure would matter more for policy than another deterioration in confidence alone because it would suggest the fuel shock was influencing beliefs beyond the immediate price increase.

The August monthly budget statement is expected to show a deficit near $404 billion after $432 billion. Its importance has increased following the proposed $5,000 payments and the renewed debate over Treasury intervention. The proposal itself is conditional on the election and congressional approval, but the budget data will update the fiscal starting point against which any new spending would be judged.

Treasury supply returns with a 20-year auction on Sept. 15 after a previous 5.204% result. The strong 30-year sale showed that investors will absorb duration at sufficiently high yields. The next test is whether that demand remains aggressive after CPI and whether Treasury’s selective buyback changes expectations for later operations.

The Sept. 16 Fed decision, economic projections and press conference remain the central policy event. Markets need to know whether an increase would be treated as a discrete response to renewed inflation or the beginning of a longer tightening sequence. Oil, producer prices and stable claims have raised the threshold for a hold; CPI will determine whether underlying inflation clears it.

The ECB’s next step is less immediate but newly live. Officials see further tightening as likely, with October possible if energy stays elevated and December offering a fuller forecast set. The market’s pricing of three additional quarter-point increases may prove excessive if wage and services inflation continue to ease, but the burden has shifted toward evidence that the energy shock will not persist.

The BOJ follows on Sept. 18. A quarter-point increase to 1.25% is almost fully priced, so guidance will determine whether Japanese yields and the yen retain their recent policy premium. Masu supported continued normalization without signaling a 50-basis-point move or an urgent follow-up in December. A routine increase with cautious guidance would challenge expectations for rapid tightening; a clear commitment to continue through the neutral range would validate a longer cycle.

Several credit events carry defined execution risk. Senegal’s Sept. 13 coupon will test the government’s pledge to maintain debt service during Common Framework negotiations. El Salvador awaits IMF board approval of its combined reviews, with a potential reduction in the coupon on its interest-only notes if approval arrives by early October. Sophos, Emeria and Merlin must convert proposed packages and creditor commitments into completed refinancings.

The common test across rates and credit is no longer whether buyers exist. The 30-year auction, corporate issuance and emerging-market transactions showed that capital remains available. The question is the compensation and protection required when oil is lifting inflation, central banks are tightening, governments are issuing heavily and the AI buildout is adding an unusually concentrated wave of private borrowing.

overall_summary.headline: Treasuries sell off and flatten as oil and firm PPI pull Fed tightening forward
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries sold off sharply as oil supply fears and firm producer inflation increased the risk of a near-term Fed response. The 2-year yield rose 15.5 basis points to 4.587%, the 10-year gained 12.2 basis points to 4.964%, and the 30-year increased 7.7 basis points to 5.367%. The 2s10s curve flattened 3.3 basis points to 37.7 basis points as markets assigned about a 70% probability to a Sept. 16 Fed increase and fully priced a move by October.

Brent climbed about 7.55% to $108.85 and WTI rose about 8.05% to $103.78 as attacks around the Strait of Hormuz and a prolonged U.S.-Iran conflict intensified supply concerns. August PPI rose 0.4% monthly and 5.4% annually; goods prices increased 1.1%, including a 24.1% jump in diesel. The 10-year breakeven rose 3 basis points, but the larger 9.2-basis-point increase in the real yield showed that tighter policy expectations accounted for most of the nominal move.

Treasury accepted $5.19 billion in its expanded 10- to 20-year buyback, below the $6 billion maximum, after rejecting less attractive offers. Private demand was stronger at the $22 billion 30-year auction, which cleared 2.7 basis points through the pre-auction yield with a record-low 2.2% dealer share, yet long yields still finished higher. The ECB also raised its deposit rate 25 basis points to 2.5%, extending the energy-driven policy repricing beyond the U.S.
